title: Bottleneck by Jun Wei
description: Explainers on the companies and industries the world can't do without.

items.title: Chipped at Work: How Close Are Bosses to Putting Tech Inside You?
items.summary: A Wisconsin company once threw a party to microchip its staff. Brain implants now let paralysed people move cursors by thought. How realistic is it that your boss asks you to get one?

items.title: The Cloth Inside the Chip: One Japanese Mill and AI's Quietest Shortage
items.summary: Under every advanced AI processor sits a sheet of woven glass. One Japanese company, founded as a silk spinner in 1918, reportedly makes about 90% of the best grade, and the queue for it is long.

items.title: Unlocked, and Still Out of Reach: The Hidden Compute in Gaming GPUs
items.summary: An open-source unlock nearly doubles the AI compute of RTX 30 and 40 graphics cards. Gamers get 0% more frames, and used prices keep climbing. Here's why the unlock helps the people who need it least.

items.title: Who Keeps the Money? The Smile Curve of AI Chips
items.summary: The world will spend about $1.5 trillion on chips this year. I followed one AI chip through eight companies to see who actually keeps the money. The answer bends a thirty-year-old rule.
